purpose: PHOIBLE features a respelling substitution may NEVER cross, because each one is the SOLE difference between two phones of this language and therefore distinguishes words in it. Derived, never listed.
derivation: minimal-pair test in feature space over the language's own inventory: for every pair of its phones, a feature that is their ONLY comparable difference is contrastive in that language

lexical_leg.why: the feature-space leg is a SUFFICIENT test only: /ɾ/~/ɾ̃/ differs on `nasal`, and `nasal` never appears as a one-feature difference because Turkish's nasal/oral contrasts (/n̪/~/d̪/, /m/~/b/) differ in several features at once. Measured, not suspected — the `nerede -> nentede` defect survived leg 1 with a green control.
lexical_leg.definition: two DIFFERENT words whose phone sequences differ at exactly ONE position prove the two phones at that position distinguish words in this language
lexical_leg.source: music_studio/data/lexicon/turkish_mfa.dict (MFA Turkish v3.0.0, CC BY 4.0), read through g2p_tr.load_lexicon() so there is one loader

refusal_rule: a substitution is refused when EITHER leg proves the pair distinguishes words: a contrastive FEATURE from leg 1, or a lexical MINIMAL PAIR from leg 2

functional_load.why: MEASURED DEFECT IN THE METRIC ITSELF, 2026-08-15: unweighted normalised Hamming distance over PHOIBLE features ranks /ɾ/~/ɾ̃/ at 0.0345 and /ɾ/~/ɹ/ at 0.1379, i.e. it calls a NASAL tap a closer match to a tap than an English approximant r is. Three successive rules were built on that metric and all three failed, because the metric was the defect. An unweighted feature distance is the naive first formula this project forbids (SUPREME LAW prohibition 6).
functional_load.definition: weight(feature) = the number of LEXICALLY PROVEN minimal pairs of this language whose phones differ on that feature (<=3 differing features, so the attribution is not diluted). A feature that distinguishes many real words carries more perceptual load in this language than one that distinguishes none.
functional_load.why_not_a_published_weight_set: PanPhon (Mortensen et al. 2016) ships hand-tuned weights for exactly this reason, but they are tuned globally rather than per language, and this platform is generic by construction (MANDATE Clause 23): every production's language derives its own weights from its own lexicon by the same procedure.

why_this_replaces_hand_written_invariant: Two invariants had been added one defect at a time (syllabicity, then spelling length) and a third defect (/ɾ/ -> /ɾ̃/) was still live. A list maintained by discipline drifts; a derivation cannot. Any language runs the same test over its own inventory.
